props.gloss_en: Rava: if he is an important person, it is permitted [to read by the lamp]
one may not read by the light of the lamp [on Shabbat]
[the reason:] lest he tilt [the lamp]
R' Yishmael ben Elisha: I will read and will not tilt
once he read, and sought to tilt [the lamp]
how great are the words of the Sages, who would say one may not read by the light of the lamp
R' Natan: he read and tilted [the lamp]
and he wrote in his notebook: I, Yishmael ben Elisha, read and tilted a lamp on Shabbat; when the Temple is rebuilt I will bring a fat sin-offering
R' Abba: R' Yishmael ben Elisha is different, since with regard to words of Torah he makes himself like a commoner
a servant examines cups and bowls by the light of the lamp
he may not examine [cups and bowls by the lamp]
here -- a servant not regularly employed [the permitting baraita; assignment per Steinsaltz]
here -- a regularly employed servant [the forbidding baraita; assignment per Steinsaltz]
both of a regular servant; that one [the permitting baraita] with a naphtha lamp [assignment per Steinsaltz]
both of a regular servant; this one [the forbidding baraita] with an oil lamp [assignment per Steinsaltz]
a servant not regularly employed, with an oil lamp: the halakha [is that he may examine]
Rav: it is the halakha, but one does not instruct so
R' Yirmeya bar Abba: it is the halakha, and one does instruct so
R' Yirmeya bar Abba came to Rav Asi's house; his servant stood and examined by the light of the lamp
Rav Asi's wife: and the Master does not do so?
Rav Asi: leave him -- he holds as his master
